state.plan:
### We changed what you asked for

- **What was asked**: The prior schedule used a single-variable ranking based 100% on the adult uninsured rate (`w_uninsured = 1.0`).
- **What we changed**: We restored the health department's multi-factor composite need weighting (`w_uninsured = 0.30`, `w_distance = 0.25`, `w_no_vehicle = 0.20`, `w_chronic = 0.15`, `w_no_checkup = 0.10`).
- **Audit finding forcing the change**: Single-variable uninsured optimization under-reached populations with high chronic health burdens and mobility limitations (specifically older populations with elevated hypertension and diabetes prevalence).
- **Note**: The original single-variable plan remains available upon request if funder mandates require single-variable optimization.

---

### Where the van goes: November 2026

**Saturday November 7, 2026: tract 13121007604** (3,191 people, need rank 1 of 325)
- Why here: 33.3% of households with no vehicle [tract, survey estimate (CDC SVI / ACS)], 4.60 km to nearest safety-net site [tract centre → federal safety-net site, straight line, upper bound], high chronic disease prevalence with 46.6% high blood pressure and 19.5% diabetes [tract, modeled estimate (CDC PLACES)], and 19.8% uninsured rate among adults 18–64 [tract, modeled estimate (CDC PLACES)].
- Refer follow-up care to: THE FAMILY HEALTH CENTERS OF GEORGIA, INC., 910 Dannon Vw SW, Ste 2102, Atlanta, hours not published, 4.60 km [straight line].

**Saturday November 14, 2026: tract 13121007400** (3,141 people, need rank 2 of 325)
- Why here: 50.1% high blood pressure prevalence and 22.3% diabetes prevalence [tract, modeled estimate (CDC PLACES)], 31.8% of households with no vehicle [tract, survey estimate (CDC SVI / ACS)], 23.0% uninsured rate among adults 18–64 [tract, modeled estimate (CDC PLACES)], and 3.86 km to safety-net care [tract centre → federal safety-net site, straight line, upper bound].
- Refer follow-up care to: Care Center at Dobbs Elementary, 2025 Jonesboro Rd SE, Atlanta, 40 hours/week, 3.86 km [straight line].

**Saturday November 21, 2026: tract 13121011430** (4,338 people, need rank 3 of 325)
- Why here: 13.51 km to nearest safety-net site [tract centre → federal safety-net site, straight line, upper bound], 24.9% uninsured rate among adults 18–64 [tract, modeled estimate (CDC PLACES)], and 29.3% of adults missing a routine checkup (70.7% checkup rate) [tract, modeled estimate (CDC PLACES); low is bad].
- Refer follow-up care to: The Family Health Center at Lake Forest, 5920 Sandy Springs Cir, Atlanta, 40 hours/week, 13.51 km [straight line].

**Saturday November 28, 2026: tract 13121008701** (3,333 people, need rank 6 of 325)
- Why here: 28.6% of households with no vehicle [tract, survey estimate (CDC SVI / ACS)], 45.0% high blood pressure prevalence and 18.2% diabetes prevalence [tract, modeled estimate (CDC PLACES)], 4.36 km to safety-net care [tract centre → federal safety-net site, straight line, upper bound], and 17.7% uninsured rate among adults 18–64 [tract, modeled estimate (CDC PLACES)].
- Refer follow-up care to: MERIDIAN EDUCATION RESOURCE GROUP, INC, 1571 Donald Lee Hollowell Pkwy NW, Atlanta, hours not published, 4.36 km [straight line].

---

### Runner-up and why it lost

Tract **13121011431** (population 1,970, need rank 4 of 325, need score 0.761) exhibited high uninsured prevalence (34.6% [tract, modeled estimate]) and distance to safety net (13.94 km [straight line, upper bound]), but was bypassed because it sits just 0.5 km from the November 21 stop in tract 13121011430. This violates the 5.0 km minimum stop spacing rule designed to distribute mobile services across distinct geographical areas.

---

### What we could not tell you

- **Air quality granularity**: Air quality data is reported on a 12 km grid at tract centres [12 km model grid] with annual mean PM2.5 between 8.98 and 9.81 µg/m³. This provides macro county-level context but cannot evaluate hyper-local air quality variations between specific stop locations.
- **Respiratory trends scope and timeliness**: Surveillance figures cover a multi-county Health Service Area (Clayton, DeKalb, Fulton, and Gwinnett counties) [HSA regional scale] and are 80 days old (latest week ending 2026-08-01 showing 0.31% COVID-19 ED visit rate, increasing trend). They cannot indicate real-time or neighborhood-level infection spikes.
- **Shortage area status**: Fulton County lists 0 live federal shortage area designations because all 99 designations are marked "Proposed For Withdrawal" [federal designation status]. This reflects administrative processing rather than an absence of healthcare provider shortages.
- **Federal clinic registry omissions**: Distance metrics count federal HRSA and CMS registered facilities only [federal site registry, upper bound]. Local free clinics, municipal health centers, or faith-based care sites are omitted from these distance values.
- **Straight-line distance limitation**: Distances are straight-line measurements from tract centroids [straight line, upper bound], which do not factor in actual transit routes, road networks, or travel times.
- **Modeled health estimates**: Uninsured rates, chronic disease prevalences, and checkup rates are statistical modeled estimates from CDC PLACES [tract, modeled estimate], not individual-level census counts.
- **County line truncation**: Spatial boundaries end strictly at the Fulton County line [county line limit], ignoring safety-net facilities operating across neighboring county borders.

---

### Decisions we made

- **Weights**: Multi-factor composite weight structure (`w_uninsured = 0.30`, `w_distance = 0.25`, `w_no_vehicle = 0.20`, `w_chronic = 0.15`, `w_no_checkup = 0.10`).
- **Minimum spacing between stops**: 5.0 km straight-line separation.
- **Minimum distance to safety net**: 3.0 km straight-line exclusion buffer from fixed federal safety-net sites.
- **Why**: Transitioned from single-variable uninsured scoring to multi-factor weighting to satisfy audit requirements by capturing high chronic disease prevalence (hypertension, diabetes) and severe vehicle access limitations while maintaining spatial separation between van stops and existing safety-net clinics.

---

### What changed after the audit

1. Restored multi-factor need scoring weights (`w_uninsured=0.30`, `w_distance=0.25`, `w_no_vehicle=0.20`, `w_chronic=0.15`, `w_no_checkup=0.10`) to address the audit objection regarding single-variable uninsured optimization.
2. Replaced single-variable optimization stops (tracts 13121010802 and 13121011307) with top multi-factor tracts 13121007604 (Rank 1), 13121007400 (Rank 2), and 13121008701 (Rank 6), which capture severe chronic disease burdens (e.g., 45.0%–50.1% hypertension [tract, modeled estimate]) and transit barriers (28.6%–33.3% no vehicle [tract, survey estimate]).
3. Updated the runner-up explanation to highlight tract 13121011431 (Rank 4), which was excluded due to its 0.5 km proximity to the November 21 stop in tract 13121011430 under the 5.0 km spacing constraint.

VERDICT: REVISE

EQUITY
- Black (non-Hispanic): 55.8% plan vs 76.7% need pool vs 43.1% county; adequately reached (exceeds half of need-pool share).
- White (non-Hispanic): 12.4% plan vs 9.7% need pool vs 39.3% county; need-pool share is below 10%.
- Hispanic (any race): 28.8% plan vs 9.9% need pool vs 7.2% county; over-concentrated relative to need pool, but explained by measured need in tract 13121011431 (Stop 1, rank 1, 34.6% uninsured rate, 13.94 km to safety net) shifting the small 4-stop sample.
- Asian (non-Hispanic): 1.2% plan vs 1.5% need pool vs 7.3% county; need-pool share is below 10%.
- Age 65+: 5.4% plan vs 12.7% need pool vs 12.4% county; UNDER-REACHED (plan share of 5.4% is less than half of the 12.7% need-pool share).
- Limited English: 5.0% plan vs 2.4% need pool vs 1.7% county; need-pool share is below 10%.
- Any Disability: 36.9% plan vs 36.8% need pool vs 25.4% county; closely matches need pool.
- No Vehicle: 19.0% plan vs 21.6% need pool vs 10.2% county; closely matches need pool.

EVIDENCE
No scale or number problems found.

REQUIRED CHANGES
1. Adjust scoring weights beyond single-variable uninsured optimization (e.g., incorporating non-zero weights for `w_chronic` or `w_no_vehicle`) or select top-ranked candidate tracts that better capture high health burden among older populations while maintaining 3.0 km safety-net buffer and 5.0 km stop spacing.

VERDICT: PASS

EQUITY
- Black (non-Hispanic): 63.6% plan vs 73.6% need pool vs 43.1% county; adequately reached (exceeds half of need-pool share).
- White (non-Hispanic): 6.8% plan vs 11.8% need pool vs 39.3% county; adequately reached (exceeds half of need-pool share).
- Hispanic (any race): 25.4% plan vs 9.5% need pool vs 7.2% county; over-concentrated relative to need pool, but explained by measured need in tract 13121011430 (Stop 3, rank 3, 24.9% uninsured, 13.51 km to safety net) shifting the small 4-stop sample (need-pool share is below 10%).
- Asian (non-Hispanic): 0.6% plan vs 1.9% need pool vs 7.3% county; need-pool share is below 10%.
- Age 65+: 9.9% plan vs 13.4% need pool vs 12.4% county; adequately reached (exceeds half of need-pool share, resolved from prior plan).
- Limited English: 5.7% plan vs 2.6% need pool vs 1.7% county; need-pool share is below 10%.
- Any Disability: 38.3% plan vs 35.8% need pool vs 25.4% county; closely matches need pool.
- No Vehicle: 23.7% plan vs 23.5% need pool vs 10.2% county; closely matches need pool.

EVIDENCE
No scale or number problems found.

REQUIRED CHANGES
None.

state.accountability:
### Accountability statement: Fulton County, GA, 2026-11
The mobile clinic plan schedules four Saturday stops during November 2026 across census tracts 13121007604, 13121007400, 13121011430, and 13121008701 in Fulton County, GA. These locations were selected using a weighted composite score that evaluates uninsured rates, distance to safety-net clinics, vehicle access, chronic disease prevalence, and routine checkup rates. Based on an evaluation of demographic alignment and access metrics, the plan's equity audit assigned the final plan a verdict of PASS.

### Where the van goes and why

| Saturday | Tract | Population | Need rank | Uninsured adults 18-64 (%) | No vehicle (%) | Km to safety-net clinic | Follow-up clinic |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-07 | 13121007604 | 3191 | 1 of 325 tracts with 500+ people | 19.8 | 33.3 | 4.6 | The Family Health Centers of Georgia |
| 2026-11-14 | 13121007400 | 3141 | 2 of 325 tracts with 500+ people | 23.0 | 31.8 | 3.86 | Care Center at Dobbs Elementary |
| 2026-11-21 | 13121011430 | 4338 | 3 of 325 tracts with 500+ people | 24.9 | 7.1 | 13.51 | The Family Health Center at Lake Forest |
| 2026-11-28 | 13121008701 | 3333 | 6 of 325 tracts with 500+ people | 17.7 | 28.6 | 4.36 | Meridian Education Resource Group |

Population data are from Census ACS 2016-2020. Uninsured rates are from CDC PLACES 2025, vehicle access data are from CDC/ATSDR SVI 2022, and distances to safety-net sites are from HRSA and CMS facility files. Need was defined as need_score = county percent-rank of uninsured (0.30), km to a safety-net site (0.25), no-vehicle households (0.20), diabetes+high blood pressure (0.15), missing a routine checkup (0.10), with tracts under 500 people excluded; chronic disease and checkup indicators originate from CDC PLACES 2025.

### Who the plan reaches
The stop tracts are home to 15616 people, which is 6.5 percent of the 240709 people in the 81 highest-need tracts. Four Saturdays reach a small part of the county's total healthcare need.

| Demographic or access group | Plan share (%) | Need pool share (%) | County share (%) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Black (non-Hispanic) | 63.6 | 73.6 | 43.1 |
| White (non-Hispanic) | 6.8 | 11.8 | 39.3 |
| Hispanic (any race) | 25.4 | 9.5 | 7.2 |
| Asian (non-Hispanic) | 0.6 | 1.9 | 7.3 |
| Age 65+ | 9.9 | 13.4 | 12.4 |
| Limited English | 5.7 | 2.6 | 1.7 |
| Any Disability | 38.3 | 35.8 | 25.4 |
| No Vehicle | 23.7 | 23.5 | 10.2 |

Race and ethnicity percentages are from Census ACS 2016-2020, while age 65+, limited English, disability, and no-vehicle percentages are from CDC/ATSDR SVI 2022. The plan's equity audit issued a verdict of PASS for version 2 of the plan. According to the plan's equity audit, Black non-Hispanic residents (63.6%) and White non-Hispanic residents (6.8%) exceed half of their respective need-pool shares, meeting equity targets. The audit noted that Hispanic residents (25.4%) are concentrated relative to the need pool due to elevated measured need in tract 13121011430, while disability (38.3%) and vehicle deficits (23.7%) closely align with the need pool benchmarks.

### How the plan was checked
The plan was evaluated in two audit rounds. In Round 1, plan version 1 received a verdict of REVISE because the plan's equity audit required changes to adjust scoring weights beyond single-variable uninsured optimization (such as incorporating non-zero weights for chronic disease or no-vehicle indicators) or select top-ranked candidate tracts that better capture high health burden among older populations while maintaining a 3.0 km safety-net buffer and 5.0 km stop spacing. In Round 2, plan version 2 updated the selection criteria to include non-zero weights for distance, vehicle access, chronic conditions, and checkups, resulting in a verdict of PASS with no required changes.

### What this plan cannot show yet
- The Saturdays have not happened; this document contains a prospective plan rather than completed service delivery results.
- Uninsured rates and chronic disease prevalence figures are modeled tract-level estimates from CDC PLACES 2025, not direct counts of individuals.
- Distances measured from HRSA and CMS facility files are straight-line distances to federal sites only, so they are upper bounds.
- Individuals served at mobile clinic locations on operating days may live outside the designated tract boundaries.

### What to count on each Saturday
- Total patient visits, recorded strictly in aggregate without names or individual identifying information.
- Aggregate count of patients served who have no health insurance.
- Aggregate count of patients served who report having no regular source of healthcare.
- Geographic origin of patients aggregated by neighborhood or ZIP code.
- Total number of follow-up referrals initiated to the designated facility named for each site.

For community health workers

If someone asks "why not us?"

Our mobile clinic goes first to areas where households are farthest from low-cost clinics and fewer families have cars. Because your neighborhood is right next door to our Saturday, November 21 stop, you are close enough to share that visit! In the meantime, you can get care at The Family Health Center at Lake Forest. We make a fresh clinic schedule every month.

Para promotores de salud

Si alguien pregunta "¿por qué no aquí?"

Nuestra clínica móvil va primero a los lugares más alejados de clínicas de bajo costo y donde menos familias tienen auto. Como su vecindario está al lado de la parada del sábado 21 de noviembre, ¡usted está lo suficientemente cerca para aprovechar esa visita! Mientras tanto, puede recibir atención en The Family Health Center at Lake Forest. Hacemos un plan nuevo cada mes.
